30:## 2. How it was built and audited
31-
32:The contract (`contracts/projects/v1.ts` 1.2.0, `contracts/workflow/reviewCompletion.schema.json`) and a design spec pinning the export format were written first; three workstreams (controller, adapter, UI) were then implemented in parallel against them, each red-first, and merged. After the merged tree was green, an adversarial audit ran six independent read-only lenses over the uncommitted diff against the PRDs (controller protocol, adapter security, export-shape consistency, PRD completeness, UI and browser tests, Python test honesty); the lenses reproduced their claims with scratch probes and mutation runs. Every finding was verified by hand and fixed (section 6 lists the behavioural ones): redaction gaps next to Markdown punctuation and `file://` URIs, a finding link that could point past the served text's truncation, a check-ID rule that would have hidden a whole workflow behind one `test:unit` policy, an invented reviewer transport for pre-slice-A plans, an interrupted native review projecting as pending, a false RUNBOOK claim about `attach`, a Ctrl-C in the reviewer launch window that stranded the session, a post-acceptance stop that was never retried, the unlinked diff `uri`, a vacuous browser assertion, an unrecorded deviation on findings grouping, and five untested guards (identity, independence, worktree and evidence re-checks, print-mode `worker`/`requirement`, best-effort pane, launch-failure receipt). Guard removals were confirmed to fail their new tests on scratch copies. The live smoke tests in section 4 found the two launch-time defects (variadic option order, permission-rule family) that neither the offline tests nor the audit could see.
33-
34:## 3. Gates run from the repository root (final pass, 2026-09-21 21:40 UTC, after the audit fixes)
35-
36-| Gate | Result |
37-| --- | --- |
38-| `npm run test:contracts` | 13 passed (10 before) |
39-| `npx --no-install tsx --test server/projects.test.ts` | 30 passed (22 before) |
40-| `npm run test:unit` | 130 passed |
41-| Python: `python -m unittest workflow.test_automatic workflow.test_interactive workflow.test_feature_launch workflow.test_sessions workflow.test_verification workflow.test_pipeline workflow.test_graph workflow.test_export` | 124 passed (59 before) |
42-| `npm run build`, `npm run lint`, `git diff --check` | clean |
--
47-
48-- Contract: the new schemas were written first with positive and negative fixtures; `npm run contracts:export` regenerated the JSON schemas; 13/13.
49:- Adapter: eight tests failed for the expected reasons against the old adapter (a 1.2.0 export was `RUN_STORAGE_INVALID`, the new routes were `NOT_FOUND`), then 28/28; two audit-driven tests (redaction spellings, served-text links, policy-label IDs, null transport; interrupted review projects as paused) brought it to 30/30.
50:- Controller: the workstream reported behavioural reds per increment (fake reviewer through `FakeSessions`, four-process reviewer-interrupt recovery, every rejected completion file, print fallback), then 108/108; the audit fixes added 15 tests (launch-window interrupts, stop retry, identity/independence/worktree/evidence refusals, print-mode finding fields, best-effort pane, launch failure, `attach` reviewer pane, recorded transport) and one prompt test, 124/124, with guard removals confirmed red on scratch copies.
51:- UI: the nine new scenarios failed first for behavioural reasons (no tablist, no task panel, no findings rows, no not-recorded sentences) with the six existing ones passing, then 15/15 in both phases; the audit fixes (group-by toggle, pinned receipt assertions, diff link by ID) kept both phases at 15/15.
52-- Live smoke test (slice A section 5), scratch run built from a copy of project-workflows-001's bundle, diff and packets with the review node driven on its own:
53-  - Attempt 1 failed in seven seconds and found a defect the offline tests could not: `--add-dir` is variadic, so the prompt that followed it was swallowed and the session started idle ("send a prompt to start"); the controller then saw the session's `blocked` state and stopped it. Fix: the prompt now follows `--permission-mode dontAsk` (single-valued) and a test pins that order; `wait_review` now treats `blocked` as "needs a human in the pane" and keeps waiting until the deadline instead of failing.
54-  - Attempt 2 (session a4c348e5, launched 20:07:35Z, pane `Claude: reviewer` attached in tab w5:tG): the prompt arrived and the reviewer read the diff, packets, contracts and screenshots, but its single `Write` of the completion file was denied: under `--permission-mode dontAsk` a rule spelled `Write(//path)` never matches. The reviewer stopped correctly rather than working around it and put its full verdict (approved, nine P2 findings) in the transcript. The controller kept waiting through the session's `done` state and, at the 20-minute deadline (1205 s), reported "Reviewer deadline exhausted; no second reviewer is launched", stopped the session with the identity re-check (`review.stop.json`), marked `automatic-review.json` `blocked` and wrote no `review.json`: the deadline path, live.
55-  - A print-mode experiment (`/tmp/permtest`, four variants) established that file writes are governed by the `Edit` rule family: `--permission-mode dontAsk --allowedTools "Edit(//abs/path)"` writes exactly that file and denies every other path, `Write(//abs/path)` matches nothing, and `acceptEdits` allows every write. The launch now uses `Edit(//<run>/review.completion.json)`; the test pins the spelling.
56-  - Attempt 3 (session 25d99bf4, 741 s): the prompt arrived, the pane attached, and the single allowed write succeeded: `review.completion.json` was written with the right run, token, bundle hash and candidate (verdict approved, eight findings with `worker` and `requirement`). The controller rejected it as a whole, fail-closed, because the reviewer had invented severity `P3` ("Review completion signal violates the schema: 'P3' is not one of ['P0', 'P1', 'P2']"), marked the receipt blocked, stopped the session with the identity re-check and wrote no `review.json`. The prompt only showed one example finding; it now spells out every allowed value (severities, dispositions, workers, verdicts, no other keys), pinned by a test.
57-  - Attempt 4 (session f36b923d, 615 s): the accept path, live. The reviewer wrote a valid `review.completion.json` (approved, eight P2 findings, each with `worker` and a `requirement` quote), the controller accepted it once the session was idle, re-checked identity, independence, worktree, bundle and diff hashes, wrote `review.json`, marked `automatic-review.json` `succeeded` with `accepted_at`, stopped the session with the identity re-check (`review.stop.json`, `stopped: true`) and left the transcript resumable (`cd <run>/review-worktree && claude --resume f36b923d-…`). `claude agents --json` listed the reviewer under `workflow-project-workflows-001-reviewer` with a UUID distinct from both workers, and a `Claude: reviewer` pane existed in the run's tab for every attempt. The export's `review` section of the scratch run derives `transport: native`, the session UUID, `reviewed_at`, the diff hash and the linked findings.
58-  - Verbatim match rate of the live reviewer's requirement quotes (PRD_RUN_INPUTS open question): 8 of 8 quotes were found verbatim in the named worker's task text, so no fuzzy matching is needed.
59-  - The reviewer's eight findings concern the already-merged candidate b5385b3 (the Projects viewer feature), not this change set; they are retained in the scratch run's `review.json` for the operator: event normalisation only emitting status/log events, phase-conditional assertions in the run-evidence scenario, thin regression coverage of the Pi/Claude experience, per-request packet loading in `listRuns`, one malformed run directory making a whole workflow unbrowsable, inconsistent redaction in `projectWorkerResult`, the app-wide `frameworkErrors` handler, and event-derived attempt numbers. Several restate the print-mode reviewer's earlier findings.
--
72-- Completion-file binding: the file binds a controller-issued `launch_token` (a UUID put into the reviewer prompt) rather than the reviewer session UUID the PRD table names, because the native session's UUID does not exist when the prompt is composed; the session identity is enforced out of band at acceptance from `review.interactive.json` against `claude agents --json` (must equal the launched session and differ from both worker UUIDs). Recorded in the PRD table and the umbrella decisions log.
73-- Findings grouping: the review panel groups by disposition (open, resolved, accepted) with a Worker column and offers a "Group by: Worker" toggle (ui, adapter, both, none, not recorded), which is how PRD_RUN_INPUTS' "findings grouped by worker" is met alongside PRD_REVIEW_RESULT's grouping by disposition.
74:- `automatic.reviewer_transport` is nullable: the export records the transport the plan pinned, or the one a recorded review actually used, and null for a run pinned before the setting that never reviewed; it never defaults to `native` (an audit found the earlier default contradicted `review.transport` for project-workflows-001).
75-- Check and scenario IDs in `runInputs` are free-form policy labels (the policy schema allows any non-empty string, e.g. `test:unit`); an earlier draft required the route-ID pattern and would have hidden a whole workflow behind one such run.
76:- Audit-driven fixes after the first green run: redaction now covers paths adjacent to Markdown punctuation and `file://` URIs; a quote links only when it also survives in the served (truncated) task text; the viewer builds the diff link from the artifact ID like every other artifact; an interrupted native review projects as `paused` rather than `pending`; `attach` adds the reviewer pane to an existing tab; a Ctrl-C in the reviewer's launch window is resumable; the post-acceptance stop is retried on resume; the identity/worktree/evidence re-checks, print-mode `worker`/`requirement` recording, the best-effort pane and the launch-failure receipt are now covered by tests.
77-- Not done: no fuzzy requirement matching (verbatim only); no live streaming; no viewer controls; the feature runs `review-result`/`run-inputs` were not launched.

    def test_a_verdict_cannot_contradict_its_own_findings(self):
        self.completion(verdict="blocked", findings=[])

        open_defect = {"severity": "P1", "message": "Unredacted path in the response", "disposition": "open",
                       "worker": "adapter", "requirement": None}
        self.completion(findings=[open_defect])
        with self.assertRaisesRegex(ValueError, "unresolved P0/P1"):
            self.read()
        self.completion(verdict="blocked", findings=[open_defect])
        self.assertEqual(self.read()["verdict"], "blocked")

    def test_symlinked_or_oversized_completion_is_never_read(self):
        self.completion()
        payload = self.root / "elsewhere.json"
        (self.root / "review.completion.json").replace(payload)
        (self.root / "review.completion.json").symlink_to(payload)
        with self.assertRaisesRegex(ValueError, "Invalid reviewer completion file"):
            self.read()
        (self.root / "review.completion.json").unlink()
        self.completion(findings=[{"severity": "P2", "message": "x" * 70000, "disposition": "open",
                                   "worker": "ui", "requirement": None}])
        with self.assertRaisesRegex(ValueError, "Invalid reviewer completion file"):
            self.read()

    def test_idle_without_a_file_times_out_without_a_second_reviewer(self):
        ticks = iter([1, 1, DEFAULTS["review_timeout_seconds"] + 1])
        with self.assertRaisesRegex(RuntimeError, "deadline exhausted"):
            wait_review(self.runtime, self.bundle, self.digest, self.token,
                        clock=lambda: next(ticks), sleep=lambda _: None)

    def test_completion_written_while_working_is_not_accepted(self):
        self.completion()

        with self.assertRaisesRegex(RuntimeError, "deadline exhausted"):
            wait_review(self.runtime, self.bundle, self.digest, self.token,
                        clock=lambda: next(ticks), sleep=lambda _: None)
        self.state = "idle"
        self.assertEqual(wait_review(self.runtime, self.bundle, self.digest, self.token, clock=lambda: 1)["verdict"], "approved")

    def test_a_missing_or_blocked_reviewer_stops_rather_than_relaunching(self):
        self.completion()
        self.runtime.sessions.locate = lambda node, rows: None
        with self.assertRaisesRegex(RuntimeError, "reconciliation required"):
            wait_review(self.runtime, self.bundle, self.digest, self.token, clock=lambda: 1)
        self.runtime.sessions.locate = lambda node, rows: {"state": "blocked"}
        with self.assertRaisesRegex(RuntimeError, "Reviewer blocked"):
            wait_review(self.runtime, self.bundle, self.digest, self.token, clock=lambda: 1)

    def test_only_an_interrupted_review_of_a_live_session_resumes(self):
        """An error recorded against the review node is not a licence to review again."""
        from .automatic import advance_failed_checks
        live = {"row": None}
        runtime = SimpleNamespace(directory=self.root, plan=self.plan, policy={},
                                  sessions=SimpleNamespace(inventory=lambda: [], locate=lambda node, rows: live["row"]))
        state = SimpleNamespace(next=("review",), tasks=[SimpleNamespace(name="review", error="interrupted")])
        self.assertFalse(advance_failed_checks(runtime, state))  # No reviewer was ever launched.
        save_json(self.root / "automatic-review.json", {"transport": "native", "status": "running"})
        self.assertFalse(advance_failed_checks(runtime, state))  # The session is gone; reconcile instead.
        live["row"] = {"state": "idle"}
        self.assertTrue(advance_failed_checks(runtime, state))
        for receipt in ({"transport": "native", "status": "blocked"}, {"transport": "native", "status": "succeeded"},
                        {"transport": "print", "status": "running"}):
            save_json(self.root / "automatic-review.json", receipt)
            self.assertFalse(advance_failed_checks(runtime, state))
        save_json(self.root / "automatic-review.json", {"transport": "native", "status": "running"})
        self.plan["automatic"]["reviewer_transport"] = "print"
        self.assertFalse(advance_failed_checks(runtime, state))
        self.plan["automatic"]["reviewer_transport"] = "native"
        # A review failure alongside a failed check is never advanced automatically.
        mixed = SimpleNamespace(next=("review", "candidate"),
                                tasks=[SimpleNamespace(name="review", error="x"), SimpleNamespace(name="candidate", error="y")])
        self.assertFalse(advance_failed_checks(runtime, mixed))

    def test_transport_defaults_to_native_and_is_bounded(self):
        self.assertEqual(transport(self.plan), "native")
        self.assertEqual(transport({"automatic": {"reviewer_transport": "print"}}), "print")
        self.assertEqual(transport({"automatic": {}}), "native")  # Runs prepared before this slice.

        with self.assertRaisesRegex(ValueError, "transport"):

def test_completion_with_unknown_or_missing_keys_fails_closed(self):

    def test_blocked_verdict_ends_the_run_with_review_recorded(self):

        self.assert_rejected(lambda item: {**item, "findings": [finding]}, "blocked the candidate")
        review = read_json(self.fixture.directory / "review.json")
        self.assertEqual((review["verdict"], review["findings"]), ("blocked", [finding]))
        self.assertEqual(read_json(self.fixture.directory / "automatic-review.json")["decision"]["verdict"], "approved")

    # ---- Launch window and post-acceptance stop -----------------------------------------------------

    def assert_launch_window_interrupt_resumes(self, bound):
        """Ctrl-C after `claude --bg` returned: the reviewer exists and keeps running; resume accepts its file."""
        f = self.fixture
        uuid, background = fixtures.FakeSessions.REVIEWER_UUID, fixtures.FakeSessions.REVIEWER_UUID[:8]
        real_launch = f.runtime.launch_reviewer
        def launch_then_interrupt(prompt, launch_token, candidate_commit):
            real_launch(prompt, launch_token, candidate_commit)  # The launch command returned: the session exists.
            if not bound:
                # Ctrl-C inside the settle poll: the launcher journaled its intent but never bound the row.
                receipt = read_json(f.directory / "review.interactive.json")
                receipt.update(session_id=None, background_id=None, status="needs_reconciliation", error="")
                save_json(f.directory / "review.interactive.json", receipt)
            raise KeyboardInterrupt  # Ctrl-C in the settle poll or the pane attach.
        with patch("workflow.automatic.wait_handoffs"), patch.object(f.runtime, "launch_reviewer", side_effect=launch_then_interrupt), \
                patch.object(f.runtime, "stop_reviewer") as stop:
            with self.assertRaises(KeyboardInterrupt):
                drive(f.runtime)
        stop.assert_not_called()
        receipt = read_json(f.directory / "automatic-review.json")
        self.assertEqual((receipt["transport"], receipt["status"]), ("native", "running"))
        self.assertNotIn("error", receipt)
        if bound:
            self.assertEqual((receipt["session_id"], receipt["background_id"]), (uuid, background))
        else:
            self.assertNotIn("session_id", receipt)
            self.assertNotIn("background_id", receipt)
        self.assertFalse((f.directory / "review.stop.json").exists())
        self.assertFalse((f.directory / "review.json").exists())
        self.assertTrue(any(event["node"] == "review" and event["status"] == "interrupted" and "NOT stopped" in event["message"]
                            and "resume with" in event["message"] for event in self.events()))
        self.assertEqual(self.reviewer_launches(), 1)
        # Resume: the same session's file is accepted; nothing is launched again.
        with patch("workflow.automatic.wait_handoffs"), patch.object(f.sessions, "run_reviewer", side_effect=AssertionError("relaunched")):
            commit = drive(f.runtime)
        self.assertEqual(git(f.repo, "rev-parse", "HEAD"), commit)
        self.assertEqual(self.reviewer_launches(), 1)
        receipt = read_json(f.directory / "automatic-review.json")
        self.assertEqual((receipt["status"], receipt["session_id"], receipt["background_id"]), ("succeeded", uuid, background))
        interactive = read_json(f.directory / "review.interactive.json")
        self.assertEqual((interactive["status"], interactive["session_id"], interactive["background_id"]), ("attached_session_available", uuid, background))
        self.assertNotIn("error", interactive)
        self.assertEqual(read_json(f.directory / "review.json")["reviewer"], uuid)
        self.assertTrue(read_json(f.directory / "review.stop.json")["stopped"])
        reconciled = [event for event in self.events() if event["node"] == "review" and "reconcil" in event["message"]]
        self.assertEqual(bool(reconciled), not bound)
        if reconciled:
            self.assertIn(uuid, reconciled[-1]["message"])

    def test_interrupt_after_launch_with_a_bound_session_resumes_the_same_reviewer(self):
        self.assert_launch_window_interrupt_resumes(bound=True)

    def test_interrupt_inside_the_settle_poll_reconciles_the_reviewer_then_resumes(self):
        self.assert_launch_window_interrupt_resumes(bound=False)

        f = self.fixture

        with patch("workflow.automatic.wait_handoffs"), patch.object(f.sessions, "run_reviewer", side_effect=AssertionError("relaunched")):
            with self.assertRaisesRegex(RuntimeError, "needs reconciliation; no automatic relaunch"):

input.summary: I read workflow/automatic.py, the review-node helpers in pipeline.py and the reviewer launch/locate/stop code in interactive.py for all three PRs, plus the PRD, each handoff, the tests that model interruption, PR 10's live smoke artifacts, the installed CLI's --help and LangGraph 1.2.11's runner. The wait/accept/binding logic is broadly similar and fail-closed in all three, but they differ sharply at the edges. PR 9's native launch cannot work live: `--add-dir <dir> <prompt>` puts the prompt after a variadic option (the CLI help says `--add-dir <directories...>`), and Write under `dontAsk` with no allow rule is denied (established by both other PRs' live runs; PR 9's own handoff names this exact risk and admits the PRD's gating smoke test was not run). PR 10 works live and stops the reviewer on every failure, but a failed post-acceptance stop discards the accepted verdict, its `wait_review` stop-recovery branch is unreachable through `review_native`, and an approved-with-open-P1 file is recorded as `verdict: approved` on a blocked run. PR 11 is the most robust: verdict made durable before the stop and the stop retried on resume, explicit launch-window Ctrl-C handling, identity re-checked against the live inventory after the wait, and the contradictory verdict normalised, all covered by tests; its remaining issues are low.
input.pr9: Control path as shipped cannot complete a live review. interactive.py:219-220 builds `--tools Read,Glob,Grep,Write --permission-mode dontAsk --add-dir <run> <prompt>`: `--add-dir <directories...>` is variadic in the installed CLI so the prompt is consumed as a directory (PR 11 saw exactly this live: session starts idle), and even with a prompt the single Write is denied under dontAsk without an allow rule (PR 10 attempt 2, PR 11's permtest; PR 9's handoff line 55 anticipates it and line 63 admits the PRD section 5 smoke test was never run). wait_review (automatic.py:196-211) fails immediately on native state `blocked` (207-208), which both other PRs found is the state a reviewer shows while waiting for a person, so the PRD's "operator answers a question" success case fails the run. On deadline/blocked/rejected file the reviewer is never stopped (288-290; documented at handoff line 58 as a decision, but a mid-turn reviewer keeps burning usage). stop_reviewer runs before the receipt is marked succeeded (281-282) and a failed stop lands in `except BaseException` → status blocked → next resume refuses ("needs reconciliation"), discarding an accepted verdict with no review.json. Strengths: zod schema with cross-field rules mirrored at 188-192, launch_token re-bound at reconcile (interactive.py run_reviewer refuses a receipt whose token differs), resumable_review refuses to resume into a vanished session (343-351), Ctrl-C mid-wait resumes correctly (4-process test, exit codes [75,130,75,0]), all rejections fail closed. Offline logic is decent; the launch and blocked-state handling make it unfit to merge for its stated purpose.
input.pr10: Works live (smoke artifacts show a real reviewer UUID bound in review.completion.json, a blocked verdict written to review.json, review.stop.json stopped). Bindings follow the PRD table literally: schema consts for version/node_id, run/bundle/candidate checked, and `reviewer_session` must equal the live inventory row's UUID and differ from both worker UUIDs (automatic.py:181-185). Accepts the file in idle/done/blocked (211-212), treating `blocked` as waiting (documented in its PRD edit). Every failure path stops the reviewer (307-314). Weaknesses: stop_session runs before finish_review (298-302) and a failed stop → `except BaseException` → status blocked → next resume refuses, so an accepted verdict is discarded (same defect as PR 9); the wait_review "recovered after stop" branch (196-198) is unreachable in practice because review_native → run_reviewer → reconcile (interactive.py:107-108,117-125) must locate a live row first, so a crash between stop and receipt=succeeded still ends in manual reconciliation and the test at test_automatic.py:572 only exercises the function in isolation; finish_review writes review.json with the reviewer's `approved` verdict even when an open P0/P1 blocks the run (271-276), which its own validate_review_record (pipeline.py) then rejects on `export`; review_resumable (216-225) accepts only status `running` while review_candidate resumes {launching, running}, and both can re-invoke a pre-check that fails outside any try (247-248), bounded only by the supervisor's 45 restarts. Solid, fail-closed, live-proven, but weaker recoverability and record consistency than PR 11.
input.pr11: Most robust of the three. Launch order pinned so the prompt follows the single-valued `--permission-mode` (interactive.py:222-226, test_interactive.py:245-249) with `--allowedTools Edit(//<run>/review.completion.json)`; live accept path proven (attempt 4). Bindings: schema consts version/node_id, run/bundle/candidate plus controller-issued launch_token (automatic.py:196-200); after the wait the live row is re-located and must equal the receipt's UUID and not be a worker UUID (332-335), then worktree, bundle and diff hashes are re-checked (336-339). Accepts only idle/done per PRD; `blocked` is noted once and waited on (219-225). Failure paths stop the reviewer (347-356). The audit fixes are real and correct: verdict made durable (review.json + receipt succeeded, 340-341) before stop_reviewer (357-363), a failed stop is retried on resume via review_candidate (236-241) and gated in drive by reviewer_stop_pending (467-479, 528, 536-539), tested at test_automatic.py:710; launch-window Ctrl-C handled for unissued/unbound/bound cases (301-315, reconcile_reviewer pipeline.py:169-181), tested at 616-670; approved-with-open-P1 normalised to `blocked` with the raw decision retained in the receipt (280-284), tested at 606-611. Nits: an interrupt before `claude --bg` was issued is marked needs_reconciliation although nothing was launched (302-307); pane attach gated on HERDR_ENV=1; run_reviewer does not assert `automatic` like the others. I found no acceptance of a bad verdict and no path that launches a second reviewer.
input.ranking_reason: PR 11 handles every edge the dimension asks about (launch-window interrupt, durable verdict before stop with retry, identity re-check after the wait, blocked-as-waiting, contradictory verdict, no second reviewer) and proved the accept path live. PR 10 proved the launch and blocked/deadline paths live and stops on failure, but discards an accepted verdict when the stop fails, carries an unreachable recovery branch, and writes a misleading review.json for approved-with-open-P1. PR 9's offline logic is comparable to PR 10's but its launch command is non-functional on the installed CLI (variadic --add-dir swallows the prompt; Write denied under dontAsk), it fails the run the moment the reviewer is `blocked`, and it never stops the reviewer on failure, with the gating smoke test admittedly unrun.

findings.title: Reviewer launch puts the prompt after variadic --add-dir, so the session starts with no task
findings.detail: run_reviewer builds the command as `... "--permission-mode", self.reviewer_permission_mode, "--add-dir", str(self.directory), prompt`. The installed CLI declares `--add-dir <directories...>` (variadic), so the prompt string is consumed as an extra directory and the native session starts idle. PR 11's live attempt 1 hit exactly this ("send a prompt to start") and its test pins the order; PR 9's test only asserts `command[command.index("--add-dir") + 1] == str(self.directory)` (test_interactive.py:189), which cannot detect the swallowed prompt. Under PR 9's wait_review an idle/blocked reviewer then either fails fast (blocked) or burns the 30-minute deadline.
findings.evidence: /home/agentops/dev/md-manager-opus/workflow/interactive.py:219-220 `"--tools", self.reviewer_tools, "--permission-mode", self.reviewer_permission_mode, "--add-dir", str(self.directory), prompt]`; `claude --help | grep add-dir` → `--add-dir <directories...>  Additional directories to allow tool access to`; PR 11 handoff section 4 attempt 1; PR 10 (interactive.py:184-186) and PR 11 (interactive.py:225-226) both place the prompt after `--permission-mode dontAsk`.

findings.title: Write is denied under dontAsk with no allow rule, so the completion file can never be written
findings.detail: The reviewer is launched with `--tools Read,Glob,Grep,Write --permission-mode dontAsk` and no `--allowedTools` rule. Both other PRs established live that dontAsk denies the Write (PR 10 smoke attempt 2: the reviewer finished its review and could not write the file; PR 11's /tmp/permtest four-variant experiment: only `Edit(//abs/path)` allows that one file). PR 9's handoff explicitly anticipates this ("single constants if the live smoke test shows dontAsk refuses that write") and admits the PRD section 5 smoke test that gates the merge was not run. Net effect: every native review under PR 9 ends at the deadline with no verdict.
findings.evidence: /home/agentops/dev/md-manager-opus/workflow/interactive.py:184-185 `reviewer_tools = "Read,Glob,Grep,Write"`, `reviewer_permission_mode = "dontAsk"`; no --allowedTools anywhere in the file (`grep -n allowedTools workflow/interactive.py` → none); docs/HANDOFF_REVIEWER_PANE.md:55 and :63 ("The controlled live smoke test (PRD section 5) has not been run"); PR 10 handoff/PRD edit: "a `Write(...)` rule is ignored by the CLI, which the first live smoke test exposed".

findings.title: Native state `blocked` fails the run immediately, defeating the PRD's operator-answers-a-question case
findings.detail: wait_review raises on `row["state"] == "blocked"` before checking for a file. PR 10 and PR 11 both observed live that a native session reports `blocked` when it has ended a turn waiting for a person (a question, or a refused action). data.summary: I read workflow/automatic.py, the review-node helpers in pipeline.py and the reviewer launch/locate/stop code in interactive.py for all three PRs, plus the PRD, each handoff, the tests that model interruption, PR 10's live smoke artifacts, the installed CLI's --help and LangGraph 1.2.11's runner. The wait/accept/binding logic is broadly similar and fail-closed in all three, but they differ sharply at the edges. PR 9's native launch cannot work live: `--add-dir <dir> <prompt>` puts the prompt after a variadic option (the CLI help says `--add-dir <directories...>`), and Write under `dontAsk` with no allow rule is denied (established by both other PRs' live runs; PR 9's own handoff names this exact risk and admits the PRD's gating smoke test was not run). PR 10 works live and stops the reviewer on every failure, but a failed post-acceptance stop discards the accepted verdict, its `wait_review` stop-recovery branch is unreachable through `review_native`, and an approved-with-open-P1 file is recorded as `verdict: approved` on a blocked run. PR 11 is the most robust: verdict made durable before the stop and the stop retried on resume, explicit launch-window Ctrl-C handling, identity re-checked against the live inventory after the wait, and the contradictory verdict normalised, all covered by tests; its remaining issues are low.
data.pr9: Control path as shipped cannot complete a live review. interactive.py:219-220 builds `--tools Read,Glob,Grep,Write --permission-mode dontAsk --add-dir <run> <prompt>`: `--add-dir <directories...>` is variadic in the installed CLI so the prompt is consumed as a directory (PR 11 saw exactly this live: session starts idle), and even with a prompt the single Write is denied under dontAsk without an allow rule (PR 10 attempt 2, PR 11's permtest; PR 9's handoff line 55 anticipates it and line 63 admits the PRD section 5 smoke test was never run). wait_review (automatic.py:196-211) fails immediately on native state `blocked` (207-208), which both other PRs found is the state a reviewer shows while waiting for a person, so the PRD's "operator answers a question" success case fails the run. On deadline/blocked/rejected file the reviewer is never stopped (288-290; documented at handoff line 58 as a decision, but a mid-turn reviewer keeps burning usage). stop_reviewer runs before the receipt is marked succeeded (281-282) and a failed stop lands in `except BaseException` → status blocked → next resume refuses ("needs reconciliation"), discarding an accepted verdict with no review.json. Strengths: zod schema with cross-field rules mirrored at 188-192, launch_token re-bound at reconcile (interactive.py run_reviewer refuses a receipt whose token differs), resumable_review refuses to resume into a vanished session (343-351), Ctrl-C mid-wait resumes correctly (4-process test, exit codes [75,130,75,0]), all rejections fail closed. Offline logic is decent; the launch and blocked-state handling make it unfit to merge for its stated purpose.
data.pr10: Works live (smoke artifacts show a real reviewer UUID bound in review.completion.json, a blocked verdict written to review.json, review.stop.json stopped). Bindings follow the PRD table literally: schema consts for version/node_id, run/bundle/candidate checked, and `reviewer_session` must equal the live inventory row's UUID and differ from both worker UUIDs (automatic.py:181-185). Accepts the file in idle/done/blocked (211-212), treating `blocked` as waiting (documented in its PRD edit). Every failure path stops the reviewer (307-314). Weaknesses: stop_session runs before finish_review (298-302) and a failed stop → `except BaseException` → status blocked → next resume refuses, so an accepted verdict is discarded (same defect as PR 9); the wait_review "recovered after stop" branch (196-198) is unreachable in practice because review_native → run_reviewer → reconcile (interactive.py:107-108,117-125) must locate a live row first, so a crash between stop and receipt=succeeded still ends in manual reconciliation and the test at test_automatic.py:572 only exercises the function in isolation; finish_review writes review.json with the reviewer's `approved` verdict even when an open P0/P1 blocks the run (271-276), which its own validate_review_record (pipeline.py) then rejects on `export`; review_resumable (216-225) accepts only status `running` while review_candidate resumes {launching, running}, and both can re-invoke a pre-check that fails outside any try (247-248), bounded only by the supervisor's 45 restarts. Solid, fail-closed, live-proven, but weaker recoverability and record consistency than PR 11.
data.pr11: Most robust of the three. Launch order pinned so the prompt follows the single-valued `--permission-mode` (interactive.py:222-226, test_interactive.py:245-249) with `--allowedTools Edit(//<run>/review.completion.json)`; live accept path proven (attempt 4). Bindings: schema consts version/node_id, run/bundle/candidate plus controller-issued launch_token (automatic.py:196-200); after the wait the live row is re-located and must equal the receipt's UUID and not be a worker UUID (332-335), then worktree, bundle and diff hashes are re-checked (336-339). Accepts only idle/done per PRD; `blocked` is noted once and waited on (219-225). Failure paths stop the reviewer (347-356). The audit fixes are real and correct: verdict made durable (review.json + receipt succeeded, 340-341) before stop_reviewer (357-363), a failed stop is retried on resume via review_candidate (236-241) and gated in drive by reviewer_stop_pending (467-479, 528, 536-539), tested at test_automatic.py:710; launch-window Ctrl-C handled for unissued/unbound/bound cases (301-315, reconcile_reviewer pipeline.py:169-181), tested at 616-670; approved-with-open-P1 normalised to `blocked` with the raw decision retained in the receipt (280-284), tested at 606-611. Nits: an interrupt before `claude --bg` was issued is marked needs_reconciliation although nothing was launched (302-307); pane attach gated on HERDR_ENV=1; run_reviewer does not assert `automatic` like the others. I found no acceptance of a bad verdict and no path that launches a second reviewer.
data.ranking_reason: PR 11 handles every edge the dimension asks about (launch-window interrupt, durable verdict before stop with retry, identity re-check after the wait, blocked-as-waiting, contradictory verdict, no second reviewer) and proved the accept path live. PR 10 proved the launch and blocked/deadline paths live and stops on failure, but discards an accepted verdict when the stop fails, carries an unreachable recovery branch, and writes a misleading review.json for approved-with-open-P1. PR 9's offline logic is comparable to PR 10's but its launch command is non-functional on the installed CLI (variadic --add-dir swallows the prompt; Write denied under dontAsk), it fails the run the moment the reviewer is `blocked`, and it never stops the reviewer on failure, with the gating smoke test admittedly unrun.

findings.title: Reviewer launch puts the prompt after variadic --add-dir, so the session starts with no task
findings.detail: run_reviewer builds the command as `... "--permission-mode", self.reviewer_permission_mode, "--add-dir", str(self.directory), prompt`. The installed CLI declares `--add-dir <directories...>` (variadic), so the prompt string is consumed as an extra directory and the native session starts idle. PR 11's live attempt 1 hit exactly this ("send a prompt to start") and its test pins the order; PR 9's test only asserts `command[command.index("--add-dir") + 1] == str(self.directory)` (test_interactive.py:189), which cannot detect the swallowed prompt. Under PR 9's wait_review an idle/blocked reviewer then either fails fast (blocked) or burns the 30-minute deadline.
findings.evidence: /home/agentops/dev/md-manager-opus/workflow/interactive.py:219-220 `"--tools", self.reviewer_tools, "--permission-mode", self.reviewer_permission_mode, "--add-dir", str(self.directory), prompt]`; `claude --help | grep add-dir` → `--add-dir <directories...>  Additional directories to allow tool access to`; PR 11 handoff section 4 attempt 1; PR 10 (interactive.py:184-186) and PR 11 (interactive.py:225-226) both place the prompt after `--permission-mode dontAsk`.

findings.title: Write is denied under dontAsk with no allow rule, so the completion file can never be written
findings.detail: The reviewer is launched with `--tools Read,Glob,Grep,Write --permission-mode dontAsk` and no `--allowedTools` rule. Both other PRs established live that dontAsk denies the Write (PR 10 smoke attempt 2: the reviewer finished its review and could not write the file; PR 11's /tmp/permtest four-variant experiment: only `Edit(//abs/path)` allows that one file). PR 9's handoff explicitly anticipates this ("single constants if the live smoke test shows dontAsk refuses that write") and admits the PRD section 5 smoke test that gates the merge was not run. Net effect: every native review under PR 9 ends at the deadline with no verdict.
findings.evidence: /home/agentops/dev/md-manager-opus/workflow/interactive.py:184-185 `reviewer_tools = "Read,Glob,Grep,Write"`, `reviewer_permission_mode = "dontAsk"`; no --allowedTools anywhere in the file (`grep -n allowedTools workflow/interactive.py` → none); docs/HANDOFF_REVIEWER_PANE.md:55 and :63 ("The controlled live smoke test (PRD section 5) has not been run"); PR 10 handoff/PRD edit: "a `Write(...)` rule is ignored by the CLI, which the first live smoke test exposed".

findings.title: Native state `blocked` fails the run immediately, defeating the PRD's operator-answers-a-question case
findings.detail: wait_review raises on `row["state"] == "blocked"` before checking for a file. PR 10 and PR 11 both observed live that a native session reports `blocked` when it has ended a turn waiting for a person (a question, or a refused action). The PRD's success criterion is that the operator can answer a question in the pane and the run resumes; under PR 9 the controller raises "Reviewer blocked; inspect quota or native error" instead, and (see the no-stop finding) leaves the session running.
findings.evidence: /home/agentops/dev/md-manager-opus/workflow/automatic.py:207-208 `if row["state"] == "blocked": raise RuntimeError("Reviewer blocked; inspect quota or native error. No billing/provider fallback.")`; test_automatic.py:254-261 pins this. Contrast PR 10 automatic.py:206-212 and PR 11 automatic.py:219-223, both documenting the live observation; docs/PRD_REVIEWER_PANE.md section 1 "the operator can answer a question the reviewer asks".

findings.title: Reviewer is never stopped on deadline, blocked state or rejected file
findings.detail: native_review's `except BaseException` only records status=blocked and re-raises; unlike drive's worker path (which calls stop_workers so no session keeps consuming usage) nothing stops the reviewer. The handoff records this as a decision ("an idle reviewer does not [consume usage]"), but at the deadline the reviewer may be mid-turn, and after a `blocked`-state failure it is left running indefinitely. PR 10 (307-314) and PR 11 (347-356) stop the reviewer with the identity re-check on every failure path.
findings.evidence: /home/agentops/dev/md-manager-opus/workflow/automatic.py:288-290 `except BaseException as error: receipt.update(status="blocked", error=str(error)); raise` (no stop call); drive's worker path at :450-459 does call runtime.stop_workers(); docs/HANDOFF_REVIEWER_PANE.md:58 "A deadline does not stop the reviewer."

findings.title: A failed post-acceptance stop discards the accepted verdict and dead-ends the run
findings.detail: Both PRs call the stop before the receipt is marked succeeded and route any stop failure into the generic `except BaseException` that sets status=blocked. On the next controller process review_candidate sees status blocked and raises "Prior reviewer invocation needs reconciliation; no automatic relaunch"; no review.json exists (PR 9) or the run cannot proceed (PR 10). A transient `claude stop` non-zero exit or an unproven termination therefore converts a valid, fully bound verdict into a manual-reconciliation case. PR 11 fixed this ordering: review.json and receipt=succeeded are written first, the stop is outside the try, and review_candidate/reviewer_stop_pending retry it on resume (tested).
findings.evidence: PR 9 /home/agentops/dev/md-manager-opus/workflow/automatic.py:281-283 `runtime.stop_reviewer()` then `receipt.update(status="succeeded", review=review)`, :288-290 blocked on any BaseException, :247-248 refuses blocked receipts on resume. PR 10 /home/agentops/dev/md-manager-high/workflow/automatic.py:298 `intent = runtime.stop_session(REVIEW_NODE)` before :302 finish_review, :307-314 blocked + one immediate re-stop, :244-246 refuses blocked receipts. PR 11 automatic.py:340-341 then :357-363, :236-241, :467-479, test_automatic.py:710.

findings.title: wait_review's stop-recovery branch is unreachable through review_native; the crash-after-stop window still needs manual reconciliation
findings.detail: wait_review returns the completion re-read against review.stop.json's session when `stopped` is true, but review_native always calls sessions.run_reviewer first, which (because review.interactive.json exists) calls reconcile → locate; a stopped session has no live row (or a row without a PID, which locate rejects with "No live native PID"), so reconcile raises "Existing launch cannot be reconciled; no automatic relaunch" before wait_review is ever reached. The recovery branch is dead code and test_stopped_reviewer_recovery_rereads_the_accepted_file only calls wait_review directly, so the test passes without the path being reachable in the graph.

findings.title: Approved-with-open-P1 is recorded as verdict `approved` on a blocked run, and PR 10's own export validator rejects that file
findings.detail: finish_review writes review.json with the reviewer's raw verdict before deciding, then raises "Independent reviewer blocked the candidate" when an unresolved P0/P1 is present. The persisted record therefore says approved while the run is blocked; report()'s export_review copies it verbatim, whereas validate_review_record (used by the new `export` action) raises "Unresolved blocking review finding" on exactly this shape. I found no test for the case (grep for 'unresolved|open P1' in workflow/test_*.py returned nothing). PR 9 rejects such a file at the schema cross-field level (no record); PR 11 normalises the record to `blocked` and keeps the raw decision in the receipt (tested).
